cards.explanation: The answer is the Spirit of God. Verse 2 puts the Spirit of God right there over the dark water, before any light shows up. Nobody else is named in the scene. Before the first word is even spoken, God is already on the job, friends.

The answer is light. In verse 3, God said, “Let there be light…” and there was light. He said it, and there it was. It's the first time God speaks in the story, and I think that's a pretty strong way to start talking, friends!

God separates them. Verse 4 says God “…separated the light from the darkness.” Then in verse 5 He gives each one a name, “day” and “night.” Naming something is a big deal, friends. I labeled cookie boxes for years and never felt that official.

God calls the darkness night. Verse 5 says, “God called the light ‘day,’ and the darkness He called ‘night.’” So God does the naming Himself, and day and night get their names right there. It's a simple pair, and I appreciate that. Some folks need three tries to name a pet goldfish.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says God made the expanse and “…separated the waters beneath it from the waters above.” So there are waters on both sides of it. Some below, some above, and the expanse sits in the middle. In verse 8 He calls it “sky.”

The word is sky. Verse 8 says, “God called the expanse ‘sky.’” That's the name He gives the space between the waters. And that wraps up the second day. Nice and short, friends, the way I like my names.

God gathers the waters so the dry land may appear. Verse 9 says, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” The waters gather, and the dry land shows up. Then in verse 10 He calls the dry land “earth.”
The answer is False. In verse 11, God says, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation…” So He tells the earth to bring forth the plants, not the seas. And verse 12 says the earth produced them.
The word is seed, friends. Verse 11 says each tree bears “…fruit with seed according to its kind.” Chocolate chips belong in my cookies, but in this verse the seed belongs in the fruit.

The lights also mark the seasons and days and years. Verse 14 says, “…and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.” So the lights in the sky are also signs for keeping track of time. Seasons, days, years, all of it. Somebody should tell my timer it has competition.

The word is day. Verse 16 says, “God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.” So the greater light is the one over the day. Big light, big daytime job, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 16 says God made the two great lights, and then adds, “And He made the stars as well.” So the sky gets stars on day four, too. It's a short line, so it's easy to blink and miss it.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 16 says God made “the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.” So the lesser light is the one over the night. And the verse adds one more thing: “And He made the stars as well.”

The word is birds. Verse 20 says, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.” So the birds get the sky, and the waters get the teeming creatures. Everybody gets a place to be, friends.

God tells them to multiply and fill the waters. Verse 22 says God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.” So the blessing comes with a command to multiply. The sea creatures fill the waters, and the birds multiply on the earth.

The answer is False. On day six, God says, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” So the call goes to the earth. The seas had their creatures on day five.

God says man will rule over them, friends. In verse 26, God says man is to “…rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air…” and over the livestock and the earth too. The list goes from the sea to the sky to the ground. That's a lot of territory to be handed, and I get nervous just managing one bakery.

The word is earth. Verse 28 says God blessed them and told them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it…” So the earth is what they're to fill. And they aren't alone in being told to multiply, as God said similar words to the creatures earlier.

The answer is seed-bearing plants and fruit. In verse 29, God says, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.” So plants and fruit are what's on the table. I'll stick with cookies, friends, but I'm sure that was a fine menu.

The answer is False, friends. In verse 30 God says, “…I have given every green plant for food.” He says it about every beast of the earth, every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth, “…everything that has the breath of life in it…” Then the verse ends with “And it was so.”

The word is very. Verse 31 says, “And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.” Earlier in the passage, God saw that things were good. Here He looks upon all that He had made, and the word is “very.” Look at that, friends.

On the seventh day, God rests from all His work. Verse 2 says, “so on that day He rested from all His work.” The work is finished, and on the seventh day He rests. It's the last day of the creation week. Friends, I take that as permission to sit down once in a while.

God blesses the seventh day and makes it holy. Verse 3 says, “…God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it…” So God does two things with this day, friends. He blesses it and He sanctifies it, which means setting it apart as holy. The verse gives the reason: “…because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.”
